binders: For every type ι in an arbitrary universe, equipped with a Fintype structure, and every real matrix A:ι×ι→ℝ.
Given a proof that A has an ι-indexed real eigenbasis, for every three vectors L,O,R in V=ℝ^ι.

There exist a function λ:ι→ℝ and a basis b=(b_p)_{p∈ι} of V over ℝ. Their existential quantifiers follow the three state quantifiers, so the witnesses may depend on A and on L,O,R; the basis witness is also inside the λ existential.
The eigenvector assertion quantifies over every p∈ι.
The conservation assertion quantifies independently over all real a,b,t for spatial integrability, all real x,s,t for temporal flux integrability, and all real a,b,s,t for the integral identity.
The initial-value assertion quantifies over every real x.
The scaling assertion quantifies over every real x,t subject to t>0.
hypotheses: ι is finite; it need not be nonempty.
A is diagonalizable over ℝ in the explicit sense that there exist μ:ι→ℝ and a real basis c of V such that A c_p=μ_p c_p for every p∈ι.
L, O, and R are arbitrary real vectors, without any relation imposed among them.
conclusions: For the chosen λ and b, A b_p=λ_p b_p for every p∈ι.
For every real a,b,t, the map x↦q(x,t) is Lebesgue interval integrable between a and b.
For every real x,s,t, the map τ↦Aq(x,τ) is Lebesgue interval integrable between s and t.
For every real a,b,s,t, ∫_a^b q(x,t) dx − ∫_a^b q(x,s) dx = ∫_s^t [Aq(a,τ)−Aq(b,τ)] dτ, with oriented vector-valued interval integrals.
For every real x, q(x,0)=L if x<0, q(x,0)=O if x=0, and q(x,0)=R if x>0.
For every real x and every t>0, q(x,t)=q(x/t,1).
mathematical_definitions: V=ℝ^ι is the finite-dimensional real vector space of functions ι→ℝ, with pointwise vector operations and its finite product normed-space structure.
(Av)(i)=Σ_{j∈ι} A(i,j)v(j). The flux is the fixed linear map F(v)=Av.
For the chosen basis b, let c_p(v) be the p-th basis coordinate of v, characterized by v=Σ_{p∈ι} c_p(v)b_p.
Define H(L,O,R;y)=L for y<0, O for y=0, and R for y>0. This definition applies to vector states or scalar coordinates.
The function in every conclusion is q:ℝ×ℝ→V given by q(x,t)=Σ_{p∈ι} h_p(x−λ_p t)b_p.
Thus each p-th basis coordinate of q uses c_p(L) when x<λ_p t, c_p(O) when x=λ_p t, and c_p(R) when x>λ_p t.

Interval integrability between a and b means integrability on both (a,b] and (b,a]. The oriented integral ∫_a^b f is the integral on (a,b] minus the integral on (b,a], with respect to real volume, that is, Lebesgue measure.
translation.proposition_plain_english: Every real square matrix indexed by a finite type that admits a real eigenbasis has the following property. For any left state L, designated origin state O, and right state R, one can choose real eigenvalues λ_p and a real eigenbasis b_p such that the explicit sum q(x,t)=Σ_p H(c_p(L),c_p(O),c_p(R);x−λ_p t)b_p satisfies an integral conservation law with flux v↦Av on every real spatial and temporal interval. Specifically, its spatial slices and its temporal flux slices are interval integrable, and the change in its spatial integral from time s to time t equals the time integral of the flux at the left endpoint minus the flux at the right endpoint. At time zero q equals L on the negative half-line, O at zero, and R on the positive half-line, exactly pointwise. At every positive time it also satisfies q(x,t)=q(x/t,1). The chosen eigenvalues and basis satisfy A b_p=λ_p b_p simultaneously with all these properties.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The matrix hypothesis excludes matrices without a complete real eigenbasis, including real matrices with only nonreal eigenvalues and real defective matrices. For such matrices the conditional assertion has no applicable hypothesis.
Neither distinctness nor ordering of eigenvalues is required. Eigenvalues may repeat, vanish, or have either sign. No symmetry of A or normalization or orthogonality of the eigenbasis is imposed.
The index type may be empty. Then V has only its zero vector, the eigenvector assertions are vacuous, the defining sum is empty, and the vector-valued conclusions are trivial.
The solution and conservation identity are defined and asserted for all real times, including negative times. Only the scaling conclusion is restricted to t>0.

No ordering assumptions a≤b or s≤t are imposed. Oriented integrals handle reversed endpoints; equal endpoints make the corresponding identities trivial, but the universal assertion also covers nondegenerate intervals.

Explicit interval integrability prevents the conservation assertion from relying solely on default values of integrals of nonintegrable functions. The assertion concerns finite intervals, not integrability on the whole real line.
The origin state is arbitrary and is used coordinate by coordinate on the lines x=λ_p t. Away from time zero, q on one such line need not equal the full vector O.
The pointwise initial-value assertion includes the exact value at x=0, and the scaling equality is also pointwise, including characteristic lines. No initial-trace limit is explicitly asserted.
The proposition does not explicitly assert differentiability, a pointwise differential equation, a test-function formulation, an entropy condition, or uniqueness among solutions.
The theorem provides an eigenbasis and the associated prescribed formula; it does not quantify over every eigenbasis or assert independence of the constructed function from the basis choice.
The quantifier order allows eigenvalue and basis witnesses to depend on the three states. It does not explicitly choose one witness pair before quantifying over all states.
